title: Signed line reductions and restriction to the derived-complete integral category
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $R_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi^n)_X$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], for any $K\in D(R)$ its derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^LR_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and the quotient-tower completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $L$ be a locally free rank-one $R$-module sheaf. Suppose every $L_n=L\otimes_R R_n$ is locally constant with finite stalks, meaning that on a pro-etale covering it is the constant sheaf associated to a finite $\mathcal O_E/\pi^n$-module. Set $L^{[0]}=R$, $L^{[m]}=L^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, and $L^{[m]}=\mathcal Hom_R(L^{[-m]},R)$ for $m<0$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]; use the same signed powers for $L_n$.

For every integer $m$ there are natural isomorphisms, compatible with quotient transitions,
$$L^{[m]}\otimes_R R_n\cong L_n^{[m]},\qquad
 (K\otimes_R^LL^{[m]})_n\cong K_n\otimes_{R_n}^LL_n^{[m]}.$$
The positive comparisons rebracket tensors, and the negative comparisons are the base-change maps on duals $\varphi\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto\overline{\varphi(x)}ab)$; these comparisons preserve evaluation.

For derived-complete $K$ [def-weil-derived-complete], the natural comparison from $K\otimes_R^LL^{[m]}$ to the specified quotient-tower completed tensor is an isomorphism, and the tensor remains derived complete. If $K$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], then both this tensor and its completed model belong to that category. Every interval $[a,b]$ containing the cohomological support [def-weil-cohomological-support] of all $K_n$ also contains the support of all the twisted reductions, and their cohomology sheaves satisfy the finite-torsion constructibility condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. The ordinary opposite-line evaluation isomorphisms restrict to this full integral category and, through the specified completion comparisons, give inverse equivalences for its completed tensor functors.

proof.text: Use the signed-power comparison/evaluation theorem to obtain b and e with PowerFormula and EvaluationFormula. Use the derived comparison theorem to obtain d, its K-flat and strict-transition normalization, and preservation of the same uniform support interval.
Use the completeness/restriction theorem for e to obtain completeness of ordinary tensor and the exact ordinary/completed restriction and evaluation clauses.

Every signed power is a line. Invertibility of ell in a residue field implies that ell is a unit in the corresponding local stalk. Apply the existing line tensor comparison theorem to that signed power and the complete input. Whiskering identifies its component with the comparison of this statement. Combine this invertibility with the completeness, reduction, support and restriction witnesses already obtained.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q45-58b0db19c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's ten steps in full against the statements of all 19 proof deps and 12 stmt deps; the delivery creates no new nodes. Admissibility: the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit, so nothing supersedes it. It is not on the dropped list and has no repair note of its own; the parent's re-split note covers only the parent. No SGA is cited, proof_deps equal the union of the step uses, and a reachability search finds no cycle. Mathematics: Steps 1-2 are elementary basis computations for the signed powers, the dual base-change map φ⊗a↦(x⊗b↦φ̄(x)ab) and evaluation, and they glue under basis change u^{±m}. Step 3 applies the ringed-topoi tensor-pullback node with u=id and R→R_n, and the comparison is compatible with transitions. Step 4: in lem-sfb-dual-tensor-adjunctions, U_Q⊣U_P, so −⊗P preserves products, and derived products are termwise (derived-limit-existence (2)). Step 5 carries the Roos triangle over with exactly the reduction-unit first map c, so no cone-uniqueness argument is needed. Steps 6-7 use the identity-field case of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison (it explicitly allows L=E and any scheme) to show that the specified zero-shifted-product augmentation into the completed tensor is an isomorphism. Step 8 keeps the same interval of cohomological support, not a Tor bound. Step 9 gets finite constructibility on the same strata from exact constant-coefficient pullback (A_n finite). Step 10 restricts the inverse equivalences through the full subcategory and conjugates by χ. Edge cases checked: m=0,±1, negative m, n=1, X=∅, K=0, unbounded K. Sources: the blueprint's sk-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free proof (3), last sentence, and Bhatt–Scholze 3.4.10/3.4.12/3.5.1/3.5.2, pp. 22-24. All nine tool_uses are generic black boxes and I accept them. Minor, not faults: the Step 5 balancing map is written out only in Step 6, and the hypothesis that L_n is locally constant is redundant. Maintainer note: the proof is 8883 characters with no new nodes. That may qualify it for a later re-split if the 2026-10-21 length rule is applied to fresh splits, but no rule binds a first split.
